purpose: Improve decision quality before any further build. Each item is a proposal, not a change that has been implemented silently. Review order: read the Questions Register, choose an option here, record the choice in the Decision Log.
how_to_review: Start with the three 'decision gates' D1-D3 below. Nothing else should be built until they are answered.
For each suggestion, read the evidence links. A suggestion that depends on missing information is marked BLOCKED and points to the question that must be answered first.
Pick one option per decision, write it in data/decision_log.json with your name, date and reason, then open a task. Undecided items stay proposed; they do not block the site.
Re-check any suggestion whose assumption is 'the market is inefficient'. The current evidence says the opposite for game markets.

decision_gates.question: Which NFL workspace is canonical?
decision_gates.why: Five earlier NFL surfaces publish different material (four dashboards plus a decision desk), and two decision registers now exist. A reader cannot tell which is current, and search authority is split across all of them.

options.name: Keep nfl-hub and freeze the other four
options.pros: One maintained surface; this hub reconciles to official standings and publishes its own limits.
options.cons: Older pages remain reachable and may contradict the hub.

options.name: Keep nfl-quant and extend it
options.pros: It already has a pipeline and pre-registered gates.
options.cons: Its lines are Week 9 and its 2026 market inputs are stale; extending it would mix two methodologies.

options.name: Publish a comparison page and keep all five
options.cons: Worst for a casual reader; the contradiction remains.

options.name: Keep nfl-hub for lines/evidence and nfl-decisions for governance, cross-link them
options.pros: Each surface keeps one job; no register is discarded.
options.cons: Two registries to maintain; the reader must know which to open.

decision_gates.recommendation: D1-a plus D1-d: nfl-hub becomes the single lines/evidence surface, nfl-decisions is kept only as its governance annex (or its unique questions are merged in and it is banner-archived). Banner the four dashboards. Do not delete anything.

decision_gates.question: Buy or license a real market feed, or stay archive-only?
decision_gates.why: With no timestamped market/player feed there is no way to measure closing-line value, price props, or validate parlay payouts. Every strategy is capped at 'research-only'.

options.name: License a commercial odds + player-prop API with historical timestamps
options.pros: Unlocks CLV, prop lines, SGP pricing and honest G7.
options.cons: Recurring cost; contract review; redistribution limits.

options.name: Stay with free archives
options.cons: No 2026 lines, no props, no parlay prices; cannot validate a real edge.

options.name: Manual price snapshots at fixed times
options.cons: Not reproducible, not auditable, and conflicts with the no-manual-input requirement.

decision_gates.recommendation: D2-a if the project is meant to produce executable lines; otherwise D2-b and accept that the output stays a research demo.

decision_gates.question: What does the leaderboard actually reward?
decision_gates.why: Rewarding raw ROI rewards luck. A strategy can top a table with 40 bets and no skill.

options.name: Reward the lower confidence bound of net ROI after gates
options.pros: Punishes small samples and variance; aligns reward with evidence.

options.name: Reward raw ROI with a minimum sample
options.cons: Still luck-dominated until n is large.

options.name: No rewards until G8 forward replication passes
options.cons: Nothing to compete over for a full season.

decision_gates.recommendation: D3-a, with the pool rolling over when no strategy qualifies. This is what the current leaderboard implements: 0 points awarded because no strategy passed.

suggestions.title: One canonical hub, four archived workspaces
suggestions.problem: nfl/, nfl-lab/, nfl-quant/, nfl-research/ and nfl-decisions/ all publish NFL material; two of them publish a decision register. They disagree, cover different weeks, and two carry dead citations.
suggestions.proposal: Make nfl-hub canonical for lines and evidence; keep nfl-decisions as a governance annex or merge its unique questions here; add a one-line banner to the four dashboards and drop them from the root nav. Do not delete them.

suggestions.title: Make the Questions Register the front door
suggestions.problem: Decisions are being made before the missing inputs are named.
suggestions.proposal: Link 'Open Questions' in the primary nav of every page and show the three decision gates on the landing page.

suggestions.title: Timestamp every number, and show staleness
suggestions.problem: Week 8 and Week 9 lines are still presented as current on older pages, with no staleness marker.
suggestions.proposal: Every table gets an 'as of' badge computed from its data file; a build fails if a slate page is older than the next kickoff.

suggestions.title: Replace point-ROI ranking with a lower-bound score
suggestions.problem: Raw ROI on a few hundred bets is mostly luck; the ladder currently has no statistically defensible ordering.
suggestions.proposal: Rank by the 5th-percentile week-clustered bootstrap ROI, with 0 for anything that fails G2/G3.

suggestions.title: Publish falsification criteria per strategy
suggestions.problem: A backtest can always be re-sliced until it looks good.
suggestions.proposal: Each strategy states in advance what result would make it be abandoned, and the pipeline refuses to re-run the holdout after a failure without a new pre-registration commit.

suggestions.title: Anchor the model to the market, not to itself
suggestions.problem: The model's margin MAE (10.39) is worse than the closing line's (9.87) on the holdout. A pure model cannot beat the line; a residual model might.
suggestions.proposal: Model the residual (actual minus closing line) with injury/rest/quarterback features, and judge it by CLV rather than by ROI on a small sample.

suggestions.title: Automate daily official-report snapshots with diffs
suggestions.problem: The injury page changes through the week and 90 minutes before kickoff. This build captured one Thursday snapshot; six players had formal designations.
suggestions.proposal: A scheduled job stores the official report daily with a timestamp and publishes a diff (new Out, upgraded to Questionable, etc.).

suggestions.title: Do not publish a starter/backup index without an official depth source
suggestions.problem: The requested 2nd/3rd/4th-string deficiency measure has no official input: NFL.com depth-chart URLs return 404.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the index blank and flagged. Either license a depth/snap-count feed or use official transaction news for named changes only (as done for quarterbacks here).

suggestions.title: Separate 'verified', 'derived' and 'assumed' at the cell level
suggestions.problem: Mixing official facts with model output in one table invites readers to treat both as equally certain.
suggestions.proposal: Three badges on every value, plus a filter. Assumed values (e.g. -110, +164 parlay payout) must be visibly assumed.

suggestions.title: Add a Decision Log page with revisit dates
suggestions.problem: Suggestions can be accepted and then forgotten; nobody knows why a choice was made.
suggestions.proposal: data/decision_log.json with id, date, decision, owner, rationale, revisit date, and a rendered page. Empty entries are shown as 'awaiting decision'.

suggestions.title: Machine-readable data next to every page
suggestions.problem: Reviewers cannot diff a table or reuse it without scraping.
suggestions.proposal: Every page links its source JSON with a schema version and a sha256.

suggestions.title: Add a link-integrity check for citations, not just internal links
suggestions.problem: Two prior-session NFL citations return 404 and were never caught.
suggestions.proposal: CI fetches every external citation and fails on 404, with an allowlist for pages that block bots.

suggestions.title: Responsible-gambling and jurisdiction review
suggestions.problem: The site discusses betting strategy; the legal status of a paid competition and of publishing picks is unresolved.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the site non-monetary and educational; add a helpline footer (present) and answer Q-13/Q-14 before any payout or 'pick' publication.

suggestions.title: Trim repository weight and duplicate raw dumps
suggestions.problem: The repository ships 53 MB of raw dumps plus four tracked .pyc files and five versions of some dashboards.
suggestions.proposal: Move raw archives to a release or external store; delete tracked bytecode; add a size budget to CI.

suggestions.title: Add search, filters and a compact print view
suggestions.problem: The hub already has 14 pages; a reviewer on a phone cannot find a team quickly.
suggestions.proposal: Client-side filter on every table, sticky headers (present), and print CSS so a page can be reviewed on paper.
